role_in_parent: Handles the second residue class modulo 8 with no need for the false arithmetic identity rejected earlier.
statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8). For each k in {1,2,...,p-1}, let I(k) be the unique integer in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and define S = { k in {1,2,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| >= floor(p/4).

domain_restrictions: p is a prime number, p > 5, and p ≡ 3 (mod 8) (hence p is odd; smallest admissible p is 11).
k ranges over integers 1,...,p-1 when defining I(k).
I(k) is taken as the integer representative in {1,...,p-1} of the modular inverse of k modulo p.
S is a subset of {1,...,p-2} (so k+1 is defined in {1,...,p-1}).
I(k+1) < I(k) is the usual strict ordering on these integer representatives.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every prime p with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8), define I:{1,...,p-1} → {1,...,p-1} by letting I(k) be the unique integer in {1,...,p-1} with k·I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p). Let S = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then the cardinality of S satisfies |S| ≥ floor(p/4).
quantifier_order: For all primes p with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8),
For each k ∈ {1,...,p-1} there exists a unique I(k) ∈ {1,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p).

variables.name: p
variables.role: universal parameter: the prime under consideration

variables.name: k
variables.role: index variable used to define inverses I(k)

variables.name: k_in_S
variables.role: index variable ranging over candidate elements of S

variables.name: I
variables.role: maps k to the multiplicative inverse representative I(k) modulo p

variables.name: S
variables.role: set of indices k with I(k+1) < I(k)

witness_dependencies: For each k ∈ {1,...,p-1}, the witness I(k) (the multiplicative inverse) exists and is unique; I(k) depends on both p and k.
S is defined from p via the function I; thus S depends on p (through I).
The numerical bound floor(p/4) depends only on p.
